about: One key sentence per founder ruling on the Engineer. `npm run engineer:rulings` checks each is on the wire — in the working tree by default, or in any saved commit with --ref (origin/main is what production builds, origin/beta is the beta site). Written 2026-09-19 after a whole round of rulings (2026-09-04) was found never to have reached main. Add a line whenever a ruling lands. `present` must appear in the file; `absent` must NOT. Whitespace and line wrapping are ignored.

rulings.ruling: Damper oil moves in 50 cSt steps
rulings.present: step: "50 cSt"

rulings.ruling: No net outranks another; choose by fit, never by wording
rulings.present: Every entry carries the same weight

rulings.ruling: A roll-centre direction can never be stated backwards (code check on every reply)
rulings.present: export function rcGuardCorrections

rulings.ruling: One question per reply, not per conversation
rulings.present: never more than one in a reply

rulings.ruling: "No change worth making" is an allowed answer
rulings.present: or instead of it when there is no change worth making

rulings.ruling: Questions are asked in the driver's words too, not only changes
rulings.present: A change, and a question, is what the driver will feel and where on the corner

rulings.ruling: Other levers: at most three, no minimum
rulings.present: then other levers that would also do it, at most three

rulings.ruling: No banned-word list (it had banned "lazy")
Feel words pass one test: would a driver say it
rulings.present: would a driver say it about how the car behaves

rulings.ruling: "More rolled-in" is not a driver's word
Corner places are entering / turning in, in the middle, exiting
rulings.present: `entering` / `turning in`, `in the middle`, `exiting`

rulings.ruling: "Loose" names a ratio: maybe the front is too aggressive
rulings.present: A balance word names a ratio, not an end

rulings.ruling: Levers are grouped into families (roll stiffness, roll centre, response)
rulings.present: Entries under a GROUP line are versions of one change

rulings.ruling: A named corner gives the phase: a hairpin is mostly the middle
rulings.present: A corner named is a phase given

rulings.ruling: A change that made the car worse everywhere: try the same lever the other way first
rulings.present: is the strongest evidence on the sheet

rulings.ruling: Two changes can share one test (physics)
rulings.present: Two changes can share one test

rulings.ruling: Paired change: the answer names the change that gets a cost back
rulings.present: the change that gets it back without touching the gain

rulings.ruling: "Contested" never reaches a driver: it goes either way
rulings.present: IT GOES EITHER WAY

rulings.ruling: Stiffer rear often feels like MORE rear grip, even in the middle
rulings.present: often feels like more rear grip and less rotation, even in the middle of the corner

rulings.ruling: Whole-car moves exist as BOTH ENDS TOGETHER lines
rulings.present: BOTH ENDS TOGETHER

rulings.ruling: Thinner oil both ends can feel like LESS overall grip
rulings.present: because it reacts so quickly it can feel like less overall grip

rulings.ruling: Exiting is always on power: never ask on/off on exit
rulings.present: Exiting is on power

rulings.ruling: A driver who named no problem is asked what problems they had, not where
rulings.present: is not asked where

rulings.ruling: "Like ice" is read as late grip, never asked about
rulings.present: is read from fact 5, never asked

rulings.ruling: Camber sits near 2 degrees and stays; reached for last
rulings.present: Where the number sits

rulings.ruling: Lowering the rear body is not a traction-roll move
rulings.present: not a traction-roll move

rulings.ruling: Initial steering is the steering geometry first
rulings.present: The first input is the geometry's before it is the grip's

rulings.ruling: Toe and bump steer before caster and Ackermann for a first-input complaint
rulings.present: The four are not equals

rulings.ruling: Nothing separates a group's knobs: name the group move with a step on each
rulings.present: give the group move with a step on each knob

rulings.ruling: A strong distinction between when the Engineer can read a car and when it can't: a car it cannot read says so, and why
rulings.present: ): NOT VISIBLE.

rulings.ruling: The Engineer sees the gearing and the motor that are on the driver's sheet
rulings.present: ENGINEER_DRIVETRAIN_KEYS.has(key)

rulings.ruling: No static rule: a knob's far end is never stated as a limit, and no drafted "usually runs" goes out until the founder gives his own numbers
rulings.absent: has little left in that lever

rulings.ruling: Only offer levers that exist on the driver's sheet

rulings.ruling: While it reads LiveRC the chat says so

rulings.ruling: What the driver suspects is a lead: help them test it, the way a competent human engineer would, never argue it away
rulings.present: What they suspect is a lead: start with the test for it

rulings.ruling: "Was that faster?" is worked out in code: each run against the one before, with the track and the tyres' age taken out

rulings.ruling: No normal-setting numbers written for the Engineer ("where does that end?"): a knob's usual value is never rendered
"Contested" never reaches a driver — not from the Engineer's instructions either (it still did in round 07)
"Contested" never reaches a driver — nor from the header over the setup priors
"Grip" on power with no end named is the rear holding on: lacking it is normally oversteer, not wheelspin ("lack of on power grip is normally oversteer")
rulings.present: lacking it is normally oversteer on power

rulings.ruling: Low grip slows the car, so more of every corner is the middle ("slower car on lower grip means the stiffer effect in the middle is a greater portion of the corner")
rulings.present: settled change is smaller, but more of every corner runs on it

rulings.ruling: What makes a tyre work harder: stiffer in roll loads it sooner and harder, toe scrubs it ("generally stiffer everything… more toe")
rulings.present: loads the tyres sooner, so they work for more

rulings.ruling: The pair loses its stock example — thinner oil was offered to a car he called hard to drive ("thinner oil would make reactivity worse")
rulings.absent: soften a bar for the middle, and thinner oil
